instructions: For each question below: (1) FULL ABLATION — using only the stem and options, with no access to the source pack, decide whether the answer can be determined. If it can, the question fails. (2) BLIND RE-ANSWER — read the pack, then choose an option without seeing the answer key. Disagreement with the key, or a defensible case for a second option, rejects the item.

questions.stem: A buyer’s purchases for the calendar year come to 950 units. What rebate is due?

options.text: 210 euros
2,280 euros
3,990 euros
6,270 euros

blocks.text: A supplier’s step rebate scheme

A wholesaler sells a single product at a list price of 60 euros per unit and operates what it calls a step rebate. At the end of each calendar year the wholesaler totals the units a buyer has bought, places that total in a band, and pays back a percentage of what the buyer spent. The scheme is not a discount at the point of sale: the buyer pays the list price on every order and receives the rebate afterwards.
The bands of the scheme, and the rate that applies to each. Units bought in the calendar year Rate fewer than 400 no rebate 400 to 899 4 per cent 900 to 1499 7 per cent 1500 or more 11 per cent
rebate = r * L * q The rebate due for a calendar year. q units bought in the calendar year L the list price of one unit r the rate of the band that q falls in

The rebate is retrospective: the band’s rate applies to every unit bought in the year, and not only to the units above the band’s lower limit. Every unit bought in the year counts towards the band, whatever price was actually paid for it. The rebate is calculated on the list price of the units, and never on a price that a separate discount has already reduced. Units returned are taken out of the year’s total on the day they are returned. A year’s purchases do not carry over. Each calendar year is banded on its own.

If a return takes the year’s total below the lower limit of a band that has already been credited, the whole of the rebate credited under that band is recovered from the buyer, and the rebate is worked out again at the band the reduced total now falls in. A return that leaves the total inside the same band changes the amount of the rebate but not the rate at which it is worked out.

questions.stem: A buyer has bought 880 units and the calendar year is almost over. The buyer is considering one further order that would take the year’s total to 900. What happens to the amount the buyer is out of pocket for the year?

options.text: It rises, by the list value of the extra units.
It rises, because the improved rate applies only to the units above the new band’s lower limit.
It falls, because the improved rate applies to everything bought in the year.
It is unchanged, because the extra rebate exactly offsets the cost of the extra units.

questions.stem: Two buyers have each been credited with a rebate, one on a year’s total of 1,520 units and the other on 1,700. Before the year ends each of them returns 40 units. According to the scheme, how do the two returns differ in their effect?

options.text: Neither rebate is withdrawn, because the band was fixed when the total passed its lower limit.
Both rebates are withdrawn and settled again.
The first buyer’s rebate is withdrawn and settled again; the second’s is not withdrawn.
The second buyer’s rebate is withdrawn and settled again; the first’s is not.

questions.stem: A buyer negotiates a one-off discount off the list price on an order of 200 units, and ends the calendar year with 620 units in total. According to the scheme, does the discounted order count towards the band, and what is its rebate worked out on?

options.text: It counts towards the band, and its rebate is worked out on the price the buyer actually paid.
It counts towards the band, and its rebate is worked out on the list price.
It does not count towards the band, and earns no rebate.
It counts towards the band, but earns no rebate, since a reduction has already been given on it.

questions.stem: A buyer expects to need 1,800 units over the next fourteen months and can place the orders whenever it suits. According to the scheme, which arrangement earns the larger rebate?

options.text: Placing all of the orders within one calendar year.
Splitting the orders evenly between the two calendar years.
Either; the rebate turns on how many units are bought, not on when.
Splitting them, so that each calendar year’s total clears the scheme’s lowest threshold.
